I don't know if this is considered spam, but if it is just downvote me I guess. I made this site while learning a little web development and wanted to share it.

[www.lueland.com](www.lueland.com)

It's modeled after a certain infamous 2004 GameFAQs spin-off, which has undergone a few changes over the years, the biggest change being the tag-based message boards.

Accounts are free, of course, but they require a valid e-mail to be activated (if there's somehow an issue with this, just let me know).

The general concept behind the site is that you can review companies and post salaries, much like Glassdoor. But there are also message boards, with the idea being that every company can have it's own sub-board (called a "tag"). Universities can also be added, so that each school has its own tag.

Then there are other more general tags, as well, like Sports, News, etc., and these can be submitted by users and managed as needed. Tags have a hierarchy, so that tags like Baseball and Football would be sub-tags of Sports, so the topic list for Sports will pull in all topics for Baseball, Football, etc. And users can filter these in and out as needed, so that topics with tags X and Y and Z can be seen, topics with X or Y or Z can be seen, topics with A and B but NOT X can be see, and so on.

And then there's the "Lue" tag ([www.lueland.com/topics/Lue](www.lueland.com/topics/Lue)), which can be used like the /v/whatever board. It's general discussion, so pretty much anything is fair game there.

Any topic can be given the "Anonymous" tag to hide all user names within that topic. Instead, each user gets a number for the duration of that topic. Attempting to guess or alluding to another user's identity is one of the few strictly enforced rules.

There's very light moderation. Only stuff like criminal activity, hacking/exploits, extremely disruptive posting, and guessing anonymous identities, etc. is actually against the rules.

So yeah, on the boards, the idea is that you can pretty much say whatever you want without having to worry about personal backlash, much like Voat but with a different board format. Feel free to call out your company or school on their problems, or talk about controversial topics without someone trying to misrepresent you in your personal life.
